§07 HANDOVER › the capstone
the capstone: the call that pulls the guard off his door is Inez's, made because the cell helped, paid or pressured her: he comes to her side and they stand together. Her debt is her need (Help clears it); the affair is her secret (Pressure threatens to expose it).

§10 PRESENTATION › payoff cut
payoff cut: plan lands → brief street-level cut → same state. Capstone has one (Inez's call lands, the guard walks off to her). More cuts + decisive shot [L].
audio = clock: bell, café door, 4:30 handover chime · surveillance click at sweep edge · patrol sound changes when it breaks route · Alert adds music layers; fight = full score · contacts confirm calls aloud · one voice per weapon · a cue when a watcher notices an agent.

hits.section: Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › Four ways to turn someone
hits.text:
Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › Four ways to turn someone
Approach (Inez, training) | Requires | Cash | Time | Trail | What it leaves |
Ask cold | Nothing | $0 | 20 s | +1 | A refusal that is remembered. Later offers cost +$10,000 and +1 Trail. |
Pay | A Watch first, where one is offered (20 s, any agent) | $70,000 | 35 s | +2 | A traceable payment. The relationship stays neutral. |
Help (clear her debt) | Need known (Listen, 30 s) | $40,000 | 35 s | +1 | Gratitude. Her bravery can grow. |
Pressure (threaten) | Need known | $0 | 25 s | +3 | Fear. Her resentment grows, and she can identify the Fixer. |
Built The approach prices are proven in play; the Watch time is a starting value. Paying Inez plus turning the driver costs $110,000 against a $100,000 purse. Helping her plus turning the driver costs $80,000. So finding things out is what pays for a second route.
Turning is private. A conversation is private: asking, paying, helping and listening have no witnesses, so onlookers learn nothing, there is no witness Trail, no change in Standing, no incident and nothing passed along. The approach keeps its own price: a payment is still traceable money, and a Loyal person still reports an approach. Pressure is different: security see a threat at any Alert, and ordinary people from Alert 2 (§05); it is remembered and passed on. A conversation never counts as loitering (§05). Spec

hits.section: Handover › G · Take the guard Spec (2/4)
hits.text:
Handover › G · Take the guard Spec
Don't loiter. The routes are laid out so no agent idles in a watcher's sight long enough to be reported (§05): the Enforcer waits out of the entrance camera's cone until the loop lands, the Scout waits out of the pickup camera's cone after listening, and nobody lingers within 3 m of the posted guard. Two careless versions show the price: the Enforcer watching the guard from 3 m (the guard grows wary, the knockout fails and the run goes loud), and the Scout idling in the pickup camera's view (reported, Alert 1). Spec
The driver can be taken too, by the same rules, but on the generated cast every chance is closed: by check-ins, by the shift change, or by Vale himself. Turn him instead (route B). The official car needs its driver; without one it waits. Unturned, he drives Vale away at 5:13 and the mission is over. The Take: at Vale's own car with his driver turned, in the service bay, it happens inside the car, with nothing to see, and ends with the Enforcer at the wheel: the driver lends him the car (§06) Decided, not built . A Take begun before 7:30 holds the driver until it ends. Any other Take has a 5 s struggle onlookers can see, and Vale walked away on foot looks wrong only to his family, or to anyone within 3 m who sees the grip. Spec

§10 PRESENTATION › conversation scene
conversation scene [S]: when an agent arrives and begins Listen, Ask, Pay, Help, Pressure, Call or Mislead, the camera cuts to a close shot of the two people and the opening lines play (at most 3 beats: the arrival line, the person's first reply, or for Listen the overheard exchange's first lines; never the reply, the result or the read, which come at landing as bubbles, so the scene can't contradict the outcome). The mission clock pauses while it plays (the player can't move) and the act's seconds run after it, as priced; the scene changes nothing the engine records, so the same seed and orders give the same result with it, skipped or never played. A cutaway, not play: hard cut in and out (a 0.12 s dip), back to exactly the view the player left (map or ground, same agent); a profile two-shot of the two people (3.6 m from the line between them, more when apart, 1.9 m high, 8° down, 35° field), else the play camera's pitch at 7 m, else, for a pair more than 6 m apart, each speaker alone cut with the bubble; never one person for the whole scene, never over a shoulder; a slow 8 % push-in, 6 % letterbox bars. Played from the ground view as from the map: both people set to idle, facing, feet planted where the engine has them; the low shots stand down the architecture cut and the silhouettes. One bubble at a time, up to 3 s each; click or Space advances, Esc or Skip ends it. Kept on screen: the clock with its pause mark, the Alert pill, the bubbles, the Skip keycap. It doesn't play in a fight or at Alert ≥ 2, if either person is down, gone or inside, while another scene plays, or in freeze or target mode. Setting: Always · First time with each person (default) · Never (bubbles only).

hits.text:
Read the street at a glance › The conversation scene Spec
When an agent arrives and begins Listen, Ask, Pay, Help, Pressure, Call or Mislead, the camera cuts to a close shot of the two people and the opening lines play: at most three beats (the arrival line, the person's first reply, or for Listen the first lines of the overheard exchange). Never the reply, the result or the Scout's read: those come when the act lands, as bubbles, so the scene can't contradict the outcome. The mission clock pauses while it plays, since the player can't move, and the act's seconds run after it, as priced. The scene changes nothing the engine records, so the same seed and orders give the same result whether it plays, is skipped or is turned off.
It is a cutaway, not play: a hard cut in and out (a 0.12 s dip), and back to exactly the view the player left (map or ground, the same agent). The framing is a profile two-shot of the two people: 3.6 m from the line between them (more when they stand apart), 1.9 m high, looking 8° down, a 35° field of view; failing that, the play camera's pitch at 7 m; failing that, for a pair more than 6 m apart, each speaker alone, cut with their bubble. It is never one person for the whole scene, and never over a shoulder, with a slow 8 % push-in and letterbox bars of 6 %. It plays the same from the ground view as from the map: both people are set to idle, facing each other, feet planted where the engine has them, and the low shots stand down the architecture cut and the silhouettes. One bubble at a time, up to 3 s each; a click or Space advances, Esc or Skip ends it. On screen stay only the clock with its pause mark, the Alert pill, the bubbles and the Skip key. It doesn't play in a fight or at Alert 2 or more, if either person is down, gone or inside, while another scene is playing, or in freeze or target mode. The setting is Always, First time with each person (the default), or Never (bubbles only).
